content_of_post_to_comment: Unpopular opinion: comprehension questions are mostly a waste of time in literature class. They turn reading into drudgery or box-checking. They make students pay attention to the wrong thing as they read. They imply that “studying” classic literature is about being able to rattle off a complete list of characters. In short, they distract from what lit class is really about: the perilous business of being a human.
